summary: Intermittent p99 stalls for identical conversational follow-ups after autoscale-down leading to streaming timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Multiple NovusDocs customers reported repeated conversational follow-ups (identical prompts) exhibiting p99 latency spikes up to 25s and streaming connection timeouts (~5s threshold). Impact: User-facing streaming timeouts causing aborted completions and degraded UX for conversational use-cases. Environment: prod (us-east-1) on Redwood hosted API, model redwood-7b-v2, traffic routed through dedicated regional pool for NovusDocs.

Observed behavior: Identical follow-up prompts (same session) that were previously sub-200ms begin to hit p99 stalls and some requests take the cold-path resulting in 20–25s token generation time and eventual client stream disconnects. This appears correlated with periods shortly after autoscaler scale-down events.

Expected behavior: Hot conversational follow-ups should hit prefix/KV cache hot-path with p99 < 500ms and streaming responses maintained.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NovusDocs test account in prod-us-east region with session pinned to redwood-7b-v2.
2) Send a short prompt to establish a session and generate a response (verify normal latency).
3) Wait for autoscaler to scale down a node (triggered by 10–15m idle window in test harness).
4) Immediately send 3 identical follow-up prompts (same session context) within 1s of each other.
5) Observe that 1–2 requests take cold-path prefix lookups leading to p99 stalls and streaming timeouts for the client at ~5s.

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Verified multiple customer reports and captured request-ids and timing. Noticed correlation with recent autoscaler scale-down events within the same pool.

SRE hypothesis: Node scale-down caused local shard->node mapping cache to become stale on remaining nodes; the prefix lookup fell back to a cold-path and triggered an expensive prefetch which was queued at low priority, delaying the KV writeback required for subsequent requests.
Reproduced in internal load test by cycling nodes (scale-down) and sending rapid follow-ups; p99 stalls reproduced 3/5 runs.

Observed that prefetch background worker uses low scheduling priority and can queue behind other IO during noisy crowding. The combination of stale shard maps + low-priority prefetch produced a window where identical prompts miss hot-path and take cold-paths for a short period after scale-down.

Root cause summary: stale local shard mapping after autoscaler-induced node removal + prefetch worker priority/policy causing delayed population of local KV cache, resulting in cold-path behavior for 'hot' follow-ups.
mitigation_and_workaround: Applied temporary customer-side and server-side mitigations: 1) Server: increased prefix-cache lease TTL for NovusDocs pool and bumped prefetch task priority to medium for 24h. 2) Routing: enabled sticky routing for sessions to prefer nodes with fresh shard maps for NovusDocs for 48h. 3) Customer-recommended: add a 200ms client-side retry for streaming handshakes to reduce observed disconnects. These changes reduced p99 from ~22s to <700ms for repeat prompts in canary testing.
resolution: Permanent fix shipped in runtime v1.9.3 (deployed 2026-02-21): 1) Introduced immediate shard-map revalidation on scale-down events for remaining nodes to avoid stale local mapping. 2) Prefetch worker now has adaptive priority: when a prefix lookup misses for a conversational session with high request rate, prefetch escalates to high-priority to populate local KV quickly. 3) Added monitoring alert 'kv.prefetch.latency > 500ms' to detect regression windows. Post-deploy verification: NovusDocs p99 for identical follow-ups returned to baseline (<500ms) and streaming disconnects ceased. Follow-up tasks: - Run broader canary across other enterprise pools for 72h. - Add an autoscaler post-condition check to force mapping re-sync and publish updated runbook.
postmortem_followup_tasks: 1) Update runbook: include explicit mapping re-sync step after scale-down (assigned SRE).
2) Expand canary to two additional geographic pools and monitor for 7 days (assigned Platform Eng).
3) Evaluate prefetch priority heuristics impact on cluster IO and revert path if regression observed (assigned Runtime Team).
4) Communicate postmortem to NovusDocs CS contact and summarize SLA credits if requested (assigned CS Lead).
